na_skrywer.blok: Die kyk bly jou eie werk
na_skrywer.voor: Moenie tussen geparkeerde karre langs die pad uitstap nie
na_skrywer.na: Moenie tussen geparkeerde karre deur die pad in stap nie
na_skrywer.rede_vinder: 'Uitstap' has no direction and 'langs die pad' can attach to the walking, so the sentence can be read as 'do not walk along the road between parked cars'; 'tussen ... deur die pad in stap' says plainly that the danger is stepping into the road from between them, which keeps the rule and does not weaken it.
na_skrywer.fout: 'uitstap' gives no direction, so the sentence does not plainly say that the danger is stepping out into the road from between parked cars
na_skrywer.rede_keurder: This is a safety instruction the writer owns, and the proposal is no fix: it drops where the cars are parked, 'deur die pad in stap' reads as walking through the road, and 'in stap' is easily read as 'instap' (getting into a vehicle).
na_skrywer.waarom: the reviewer sent it to the writer

laat_vaar_vorige.voor: Loop op die sypaadjie waar daar een
laat_vaar_vorige.na: Loop op die sypaadjie as daar een
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: 'As daar een is' (if there is one) reads more naturally than 'waar daar een is' here.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: 'Waar daar een langs die pad is' reads naturally already, and this is a safety instruction, so a sideways word swap is not worth making.

laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: A pavement runs alongside a road, so 'langs' is the natural preposition.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: 'By baie paaie' is acceptable and an editor would let it pass. 'Langs' would also repeat the 'langs die pad' in the sentence just before it.

laat_vaar_vorige.voor: Kyk eers na regs en dan na links
laat_vaar_vorige.na: Kyk na regs, dan na links
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: Removes a second 'eers' straight after the previous sentence's 'eers' and avoids the chain 'en dan ... en dan'.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: In the kerb drill, 'eers' marks which side to look first. Removing it weakens the order of a safety instruction.

laat_vaar_vorige.voor: Op 'n fiets ry jy op die pad saam met die karre, aan die linkerkant
laat_vaar_vorige.na: Op 'n fiets ry jy saam met die karre aan die linkerkant van die pad
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: The afterthought ', aan die linkerkant' reads awkwardly; one phrase says the same.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: The original stresses 'op die pad' (on the road, not the pavement) and then the side. The merged phrase weakens that stress in a safety instruction and could be read as 'the cars on the left'.

laat_vaar_vorige.voor: sorg dat die fiets se remme
laat_vaar_vorige.na: sorg dat jou fiets se remme
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: The block addresses the learner directly, so 'jou fiets' fits better than 'die fiets'.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: This is a sideways move. 'Die fiets' points back to ''n fiets' and also covers a bike the child does not own.

laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: 'Dra' calques English 'wear a seatbelt'; Afrikaans fastens it: 'maak vas'. The instruction stays the same.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: 'Dra die sitplekgordel' is established Afrikaans road-safety wording, and 'maak vas' narrows the instruction from wearing the belt for the whole trip to buckling it once.

laat_vaar_vorige.voor: Klim uit aan die kant van die sypaadjie
laat_vaar_vorige.na: Klim uit aan die sypaadjie se kant
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: Mirrors 'aan die verkeer se kant' later in the same sentence, making the contrast clearer.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: This is a sideways rewording of a safety instruction that already reads clearly.

laat_vaar_vorige.voor: Steek die spoor net oor by 'n brug of by 'n oorgang
laat_vaar_vorige.na: Steek die spoor net by 'n brug of by 'n oorgang oor
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: The separable particle 'oor' naturally goes to the end of the clause.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: Putting the particle before the 'by' phrase is natural spoken Afrikaans and matches 'Steek oor by 'n sebrapad' earlier in the lesson. It is a sideways move in a safety instruction.

laat_vaar_vorige.na: aan die buitekant van die trein vashou
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: 'Die buitekant' has no clear reference after 'n oop deur'; naming the train makes it clear.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: Within a block headed 'By die trein', 'aan die buitekant' is clear. Adding words to a safety instruction is a sideways move here.

laat_vaar_vorige.voor: Die gordel wat jou in jou sitplek in 'n voertuig hou
laat_vaar_vorige.na: Die gordel wat jou in 'n voertuig in jou sitplek vashou
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: 'Vashou' says what the belt does; 'hou' on its own is vague.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: This is a glossary definition, and 'wat jou in jou sitplek hou' is already clear, correct Afrikaans, so there is no real fault to send to the writer.

laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: For the order of one's own actions Afrikaans uses the adverb 'eers'; 'eerste' ranks against others, and the sentence before already uses 'eers' this way.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: Lateral move: 'eerste soontoe' naturally ranks this direction before the others (as in 'watter kant toe kyk jy eerste?'), the original reads well, and 'eers' would be the third 'eers' in two sentences of a checked safety explanation.

laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: 'die hand' is wooden in an instruction addressed to 'jy'; 'jou hand' is the natural form and changes nothing in the rule.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: 'die hand' points to the one hand that signalled, while 'jou hand' is vaguer with two hands on the handlebar, so this is at best a lateral move in a safety instruction.

laat_vaar_vorige.blok: Die kyk bly jou eie werk
laat_vaar_vorige.voor: en die kyk bly jou werk
laat_vaar_vorige.na: en jy moet self bly kyk
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: 'Die kyk' as a noun for the act of looking is wooden in running Afrikaans; the verb form says the same thing naturally (the heading, which cannot change, keeps its own wording).
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: The body sentence deliberately echoes the protected heading 'Die kyk bly jou eie werk', and rewording this road-safety rule loses that echo and changes a checked safety instruction.
